ev.q: An estimated 11% of the U.S. population aged ≥6 years are seropositive for toxoplasmosis
Among six states that participated in a surveillance evaluation, case definitions varied considerably

public_health_question.v: How do the states where toxoplasmosis is reportable collect, define, investigate and use surveillance data for human toxoplasmosis?

ev.q: To better understand how surveillance data are collected and used, reviews of state-level toxoplasmosis surveillance were conducted
Public Health Surveillance and Reporting for Human Toxoplasmosis — Six States, 2021
Among six states that participated in a surveillance evaluation, case definitions varied considerably
using semistructured interviews with health officials in six states
Public Health Surveillance and Reporting for Human Toxoplasmosis — Six States, 2021

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed; the report is a qualitative review of state surveillance case definitions and processes.

notes: A qualitative surveillance-system evaluation based on interviews and state case definitions; its only outcome quantity (11% seroprevalence) is cited from NHANES, so data_focus is limited rather than none. The CSTE State Reportable Conditions Assessment query tool was used only to identify reportable states (a roster), so it is not listed as a data source.
